title: Mosel
description: Some of the world's steepest vineyards: light, racy Riesling grown on slate above a winding river.
L: The Mosel river rises in France and winds north-east through western Germany to join the Rhine at Koblenz. Its German wine region follows about 240 km of loops and bends, with vineyards on the steep banks. It has about 8,700 hectares. It includes two tributaries, the Saar and the Ruwer.

The Mosel lies at about 50 degrees north, one of the coolest quality wine regions in the world. Average growing season temperatures are low, and ripening is a challenge. The river helps: it moderates temperature, reflects sunlight onto the slopes, and its loops create south-facing banks that catch every hour of sun.
How does the river help Mosel vineyards?
It moderates temperature and reflects sunlight
Water stores heat and reflects light onto the slopes.

The Mosel is often divided into the Upper Mosel, near Luxembourg, on limestone, growing Elbling; the Middle Mosel, Mittelmosel, the heart, with famous villages like Piesport, Bernkastel, Graach, Wehlen and Ürzig; and the Lower Mosel, Terrassenmosel, near Koblenz, with very steep terraces. The Saar and Ruwer join in the south.
The Middle Mosel is home to villages like Bernkastel and Wehlen.
Yes. It's the heart of the region.
The Mosel winds 240 km through western Germany
It's very cool, at about 50 degrees north
The river and its loops help ripening on south-facing banks

Riesling covers about 62% of the Mosel's vineyards, and almost all its fine wine. It buds and ripens late, tolerates cold winters, and keeps high acidity. On the Mosel's slate, it gives light, delicate wines with green apple, peach, citrus, flowers and a smoky, slatey mineral edge.

Müller-Thurgau, a cross created in 1882, is grown on flatter land. Elbling, an ancient grape, grows in the Upper Mosel, often for sparkling Sekt. Pinot Noir and Pinot Blanc are increasing. Mosel Riesling is famous for low alcohol, often 7.5 to 10%, with sugar balanced by fierce acidity; but dry styles are growing.
Match each grape to its role.
A Mosel Riesling Kabinett at 8% alcohol shows how wine can be intensely flavoured without weight.
Why does Mosel Riesling often have low alcohol?
Grapes ripen slowly, and some sugar is left in the wine
It's made from unripe white grapes only
Cool ripening and residual sugar keep alcohol low.
Riesling is about 62% of vineyards and most fine wine
Mosel Riesling is light, high in acidity, often off-dry
Müller-Thurgau and Elbling play supporting roles

The Mosel has some of the steepest vineyards in the world. The Bremmer Calmont, in the Lower Mosel, reaches about 65 degrees, often called Europe's steepest. Vines are trained on single poles, Einzelpfahl, and work is by hand, sometimes with monorails. Steepness gives more sun and drainage, but costs are high.

Most top vineyards are on Devonian slate, grey, blue or red. Slate drains well, absorbs heat by day and releases it at night, helping ripening. Broken slate on the surface reflects light. Many link slate to the Mosel's mineral, smoky character, though the science is debated; its effect on heat and drainage is clear.
Slate stores heat and drains well
How does slate help Mosel vineyards?
It absorbs and releases heat and drains well
It holds water like a sponge
Heat storage and drainage help ripening.

Famous vineyards include Wehlener Sonnenuhr, with its sundial; Bernkasteler Doctor, among Germany's most expensive; Ürziger Würzgarten, on red slate; Graacher Himmelreich; and Piesporter Goldtröpfchen. Labels name the village plus the vineyard, like Wehlener Sonnenuhr, from Wehlen.
Clos de Vougeot is in Burgundy.
The Mosel has some of the world's steepest vineyards
Slate stores heat and drains well
Labels name village plus vineyard, like Wehlener Sonnenuhr

German Prädikatswein is graded by grape sugar at harvest, measured in Oechsle: Kabinett, Spätlese, Auslese, Beerenauslese, BA, Eiswein and Trockenbeerenauslese, TBA. The levels show ripeness, not the wine's final sweetness. In the Mosel, Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese are often made off-dry or sweet, by tradition.

Trocken means dry, up to 9 g/l of sugar; halbtrocken, off-dry, up to 18 g/l; feinherb, an unofficial off-dry term. Without these words, a Mosel Prädikat wine is usually fruity-sweet, fruchtsüss. The high acidity, often 8 to 10 g/l, balances the sugar, so even sweet wines taste fresh.
Order the Prädikat levels from least to most ripe.
Each level demands riper grapes at harvest.

In great years, the Mosel makes Beerenauslese, Trockenbeerenauslese and Eiswein, from botrytised or frozen grapes, with intense sweetness and acidity. Auctions, like the Grosser Ring auction in Trier, sell rare sweet wines for high prices. These wines age for decades.
BA, TBA and Eiswein in great years
What does trocken on a German label mean?
Prädikat levels show ripeness, from Kabinett to TBA
Trocken means dry; without it, Mosel Prädikats are often sweet

The Saar joins the Mosel near Trier. It's cooler and windier than the Middle Mosel, and for centuries grapes ripened fully only in good years. In warm years, its Rieslings are among the most precise and electric in the world, with steely acidity. Scharzhofberg, owned largely by Egon Müller, is its most famous vineyard.

The Ruwer is a small tributary near Trier, with only a few estates. Its wines are delicate, floral and racy. Maximin Grünhaus and Karthäuserhofberg are famous estates, both former monastic properties. Like the Saar, it was officially part of the Mosel-Saar-Ruwer region until 2007, when the region was renamed simply Mosel.
How do the Saar and Ruwer differ from the Middle Mosel?
Cooler conditions give steely, precise Riesling.

Warmer summers since the 1990s have helped the Saar and Ruwer ripen grapes more reliably. What was once a marginal climate now gives balanced wines more often. This has made these cool tributaries even more prized for freshness.
The region was renamed from Mosel-Saar-Ruwer to Mosel in 2007.
The Saar is cool and windy, home of Scharzhofberg
The Ruwer is small, delicate and floral
Warmer summers have helped them ripen more reliably
Reading the Mosel and eating with it

A Mosel label shows the producer, the village plus vineyard, like Bernkasteler Doctor, the grape, the Prädikat, like Spätlese, the vintage and sometimes trocken. VDP estates use their own classification: Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage and Grosse Lage, with GG, Grosses Gewächs, for dry top wines. The AP number shows official testing.

Off-dry Mosel Kabinett suits spicy Asian food, like Thai and Sichuan, and smoked fish. Dry Riesling suits trout, pork and sauerkraut. Spätlese suits roast pork with apples. Sweet Auslese and BA suit fruit desserts, foie gras and blue cheese. Serve at 7 to 10 degrees.
Which food suits an off-dry Mosel Kabinett?
Sugar and acidity calm chilli heat.
Mosel Riesling ages remarkably. A 20-year-old Spätlese often tastes less sweet and more complex than a young one.
Labels show village, vineyard and Prädikat
Kabinett suits spicy food; Auslese suits desserts
